202.description: Accepted into bounded memory; not a durability acknowledgement.

422.description: Invalid event, ownership, identity, envelope or payload; input is never echoed.

event_name.description: FE-owned name in the frozen V3 registry.

properties.description: Frozen V3 envelope + per-event allowlist; runtime validated.

get.description:
Deep health check: 200 only when the DB and Redis both answer.
Used by the docker-compose healthcheck and load-balancer probes.

Which code and which schema this instance runs; null revision when the
database has no alembic_version table (e.g. schema built without Alembic).

post.description:
Issue narrow-scoped temporary OSS credentials.

The returned token can ONLY (a) hit `users/<this-user>/<action>/` prefix
of the named bucket, (b) for the requested verb, (c) for the configured
TTL. iOS uses this to upload originals directly without ever holding a
permanent AccessKey — server never sees the bytes (saves bandwidth).

Record that the user wore this item (no outfit context), for
`worn_date` (defaults to the user's local date).

Updates last_worn_at and wear_count on the item so insights / detail
screens reflect the real-world wear immediately. Also emits a
RecommendationEvent for future preference learning.

get.description:
Cold-start feasibility gate.

Returns a structured verdict that tells the FE whether the user has enough
wardrobe to show an outfit. The gate result itself is not cached (called
once on FE V2 activation, cheap DB hit).

post.description:
Phase D3 — user-initiated refresh. Writes a new revision; old revision
rows + their wear/feedback references are preserved. Rate-limited per
`TODAY_REFRESH_DAILY_LIMIT` (default 3/d incl. background rev-1).

BE#81 — general passive-learning event ingestion. Append-only; distinct
from the explicit feedback endpoints above (which stay backward compatible).

M19 — async PDF / magazine multi-page style ingest.

`ENABLE_PDF_STYLE_INGEST` is an upload-ingest kill switch (default off).
Flag=off → gate-and-reject (no row created). Convention: data-always-persists
applies to user-triggered flags (ENABLE_TODAY_REFRESH etc.), not to this
upload-ingest kill-switch where creating a row with no processing is meaningless.
`estimated_pages` is best-effort 0 at enqueue: the real count is only known
once the worker downloads and rasterizes the PDF, and blocking the request on
an OSS fetch would defeat the async design.

404.description: `source_asset_id` is not an object key under the caller's own prefix.
No such candidate for this user (a foreign candidate answers 404, not 403).

post.description:
Produce — or return the existing — structured decision (contract §5.3).

Idempotent per candidate: repeated calls replay the first decision instead
of re-evaluating, so the explanation a user saw cannot change under them.
A `parse_failed` candidate is decidable too; it reaches
`insufficient_information` rather than an error (contract §5.2).

404.description: No such candidate for this user (a foreign candidate answers 404, not 403).

get.description:
Replay a decision from its immutable snapshots (contract §5.3).

Nothing is recomputed: the copy, the reasons and the compared item ids come
out of the frozen snapshot, so later wardrobe changes never rewrite an old
explanation. Only `image_url` is materialized here — same rule as the POST.

404.description: No such decision for this user (a foreign decision answers 404, not 403).
No such decision for this user (a foreign decision answers 404, not 403).

429.description: `4091 STATE_CONFLICT`; `data.reason` is `daily_budget_exhausted` (the per-user daily try-on budget is spent, `ENABLE_COST_GUARD`) or `retry_budget_exhausted` (this generation has used its bounded retry allowance and will not be re-attempted). Both are retryable states for the client, on different horizons: tomorrow, and never for this preview.

404.description: No static try-on render with this id belongs to this user. A foreign asset, a missing asset and the caller's own non-try-on asset are indistinguishable here (contract §3).

422.description: Verdict or aspect outside the frozen vocabulary, or an extra field.

delete.description:
Disable and delete (contract §4.2).

`purge_derived` is a **required** query parameter with no default — declared
here without one, so omitting it is a 422 rather than a silent choice about
somebody's photos. V3_SPEC §13.5 requires being explicit about whether
derived assets are deleted too, which means the caller has to say.

What it governs today, and what it does not yet, is documented in
`app/application/avatar/delete_avatar.py`.

post.description:
Accept or decline one candidate (contract §4.2).

Acceptance 1 lands here: `record_consent` writes the copy version and the
decision timestamp onto the asset *and* the profile, and the table's CHECK
constraints refuse a decided consent with no timestamp or an accepted one
with no version — so a recorded consent cannot be missing either field.

The two shape rules are enforced before the transition, as business errors
rather than FastAPI 422s: accepting requires a copy version, and declining
must not carry one (a "declined under version X" record would imply the user
agreed to something).

Source C — a photo the user deliberately took or picked for this purpose.

Registration is not consent. This hands the photo to V3-012's detection with
`PREVIEW_REQUEST`, which assesses it and — if it qualifies — offers it as a
`candidate`; the user then accepts through the consent endpoint. Two steps,
because V3_SPEC §7.1's source-B rule is that material never becomes a person
reference implicitly, and a deliberate upload does not change who has to say
yes. It also means this endpoint cannot be used to skip the consent record
that acceptance 1 requires.

`PREVIEW_REQUEST` is the trigger V3-012 built for exactly this caller: it
widens which *users* may be asked (a `disabled` profile can be offered
material again, contract §4.1's `disabled → preparing` path) without widening
which *photos* may be re-offered — a previously declined photo stays declined.
Until this endpoint existed, that trigger had no caller, which V3-012
recorded as an open risk.
Start preparation from a consented source (contract §4.2).

Prepare a new version; atomic swap on success (contract §4.2).

Same machinery as `prepare`, different precondition — and the swap itself is
`AvatarLifecycle.activate_version`, reached only after the provider
succeeded, which is what makes "replace failure keeps the previous version
active" true by construction rather than by a compensating write.

get.description:
List async jobs filtered by status (default `dead`).

Bounded by `limit<=200` so a single misconfigured query can't pull the
whole table into memory.

post.description:
One-shot repair for legacy wardrobe items imported before naming
localization (BE#30): AI-named rows without `localized_names` render their
raw (usually English) title on every surface. Each call batches `limit`
items into one LLM request producing zh-CN/en-US name pairs; user-renamed
items are never touched. Call repeatedly until `remaining` is 0.

get.description:
User-visible token / call usage for today. Always returns a payload —
when ENABLE_COST_GUARD is off the `limit` field is the unused default
(so the client can pre-render the UI before the operator turns the
feature on).

post.description:
PIPL DSAR — kick off an asynchronous export of the user's personal
data. Bundle path runs as a `user_export` async-job; the user receives
a download link (push / email) when ready. Idempotent per pending
request: re-calling while one is in flight returns the same job_id, with
its real `status`; a `dead` job is replaced by a fresh one.

get.description:
Poll the status of a previously requested data export job.
Returns 404 when the job_id does not belong to this user.

delete.description:
PIPL-aware account deactivation. Soft-deletes immediately; hard-purge
fires after the grace window via the user_purge async-job worker.

Idempotent — calling twice on an already-deactivated account is OK and
returns the same scheduled_purge_at.

post.description:
Same removal as DELETE, but audited distinctly — "this is wrong" is a
correction signal future learning can weigh, not just a removal.

schema.title: Response Ask History V1 Ask History Get

post.description:
BE#86 — record a feedback signal against an Ask session.

Loads the AskSession and enforces ownership (404 on missing or foreign —
never reveals existence). Writes a RecommendationEvent with source
"ask_feedback" so the event stream accumulates per-session signals.
Idempotent: repeated calls append new events (same as Today feedback).

AppliedContextResponse.title: AppliedContextResponse
AppliedContextResponse.description:
BE#78 — echoes the context override that shaped this refresh, so FE can
explain why the outfit changed.

AskItemRefSnapshot.title: AskItemRefSnapshot
AskItemRefSnapshot.description:
BE#29 — denormalized card for a referenced wardrobe item so the client
can render related items without a per-id detail fetch. Only the current
user's accessible, non-deleted items appear; `thumbnail_url` is signed at
request time (never a persisted TTL-bound URL).

AskTripIntent.title: AskTripIntent
AskTripIntent.description:
BE#115 — present only when the structured answer detected a multi-day
trip question; the FE uses it to offer the packing-list handoff.

AvatarCandidateModel.title: AvatarCandidateModel
AvatarCandidateModel.description:
`candidate` — material awaiting a consent decision; null while preparing.

Not restricted to `status=candidate`: a revoked or already-ready profile can
carry one too, which is what makes §4.1's `disabled → preparing` re-enable
and §4.2's `replace` from a new photo reachable. `_render_profile` carries
the full rationale.

AvatarConsentModel.title: AvatarConsentModel
AvatarConsentModel.description:
`consent` — null until first consent.

Together these two fields are V3-013 acceptance 1 ("Consent version and
timestamp are recorded") as seen from outside: the version is the copy the
user actually accepted, and the timestamp is when.

AvatarConsentRequest.title: AvatarConsentRequest
AvatarConsentRequest.description:
`POST …/consent` body: `{"accept": true|false}`.

`consent_version` is required when accepting and forbidden otherwise — the
frozen §4.2 rule ("`accept=true` requires the consent copy version"). It is
validated in the router rather than by a model validator so the refusal
carries the same `4001 VALIDATION_ERROR` envelope as every other business
rule, instead of FastAPI's raw 422 shape.

Bounded at 64 characters to match `avatar_source_assets.consent_version`, so
an over-long value is refused at the edge rather than truncated by the
database.

AvatarUploadRegistrationRequest.title: AvatarUploadRegistrationRequest
AvatarUploadRegistrationRequest.description:
`POST /v1/avatar-profile/uploads` — source C (V3_SPEC §7.1).

Carries the reference to an object the client has *already* uploaded through
the existing presign flow, which is what contract §4.2 specifies ("Reuses the
existing presign upload flow; body carries the uploaded asset reference").
Either the `object_key` from `POST /v1/uploads/presign` or the `file_url` it
returned alongside — clients hold both, and accepting only one of them would
make this endpoint depend on which field a client happened to keep.

Ownership of whatever this resolves to is enforced in the router: this is a
free-form client-supplied reference, the exact shape of the cross-user read
V3-012's round-3 review found.

ClosetComparisonModel.title: ClosetComparisonModel
ClosetComparisonModel.description: V3_SPEC §5.4 layer 3 — what the wardrobe already covers.

ComparisonItemModel.title: ComparisonItemModel
ComparisonItemModel.description:
One row of `closet_comparison.similar_items`.

`image_url` is a short-lived signed URL materialized at read time and never
persisted (V3_SPEC §13.5); it is `null` when the item has no image or when
signing is unavailable, which is a display detail rather than an error.

ConfirmItemInput.title: ConfirmItemInput
ConfirmItemInput.description:
BE#25 — one candidate (keyed by `temp_item_id`) the client elected to
import, carrying its edited form fields. Typed values win over the AI guess.

ContextOverrideRequest.title: ContextOverrideRequest
ContextOverrideRequest.description: BE#78 — a chip or free-text Today context override for one refresh.

source_type.title: Source Type
source_type.description: Where the candidate came from. `share_link`/`ask_link` require `source_url`; `screenshot`/`order_image` require `source_asset_id`.

source_asset_id.title: Source Asset Id
source_asset_id.description: For `screenshot` / `order_image`: the stable `object_key` returned by `POST /v1/uploads/presign` (e.g. `users/<user_id>/<uuid>.jpg`), NOT a UUID and NOT the TTL-bound `file_url`. This service has no generic asset table, so the object key IS the asset reference; it must be under the caller's own `users/<user_id>/` prefix.

DecisionReasonModel.title: DecisionReasonModel
DecisionReasonModel.description:
One of the 2–3 reasons, ordered by importance.

`text` is server-rendered display copy: contract §5.3 forbids the client to
synthesize it, and it is frozen into the decision snapshot so a historical
explanation never changes wording. `adoption_history` is part of the frozen
vocabulary but is not emitted in P0 (no loaded projection carries wear
counts) — a client must still tolerate it.

concern.title: Concern
concern.description: What the user is unsure about. Only grades how prominently a visual preview is offered (`volume`/`color` are the two a static preview can answer); it never changes the decision itself.

DecisionRequest.title: DecisionRequest
DecisionRequest.description: Contract §5.3 request body. Optional — an omitted body means `none`.

I18nMessage.title: I18nMessage
I18nMessage.description:
A renderable explanation token.

- `key` is a stable dotted identifier (`obstacle.laundry`, `prep.iron`).
  Clients lookup their own locale bundle by this key.
- `params` is a flat string-keyed dict; values must be JSON-serializable
  and already client-safe (no internal IDs, no PII).
- `fallback_text` is the server-rendered zh-CN string. REQUIRED.
  Clients without a locale bundle for `key` display this verbatim.

wear_history_count.title: Wear History Count
wear_history_count.description: Sum of item-level wear counts over live items, including manual item wears. Not the number of outfit records: compare `GET /v1/outfit-history` `total`.

total.title: Total
total.description: Number of outfit-level wear records (one per outfit worn on a day). Not comparable to insights `wear_history_count`, which sums item-level wears including manual item wears.

PackingPlan.title: PackingPlan
PackingPlan.description: BE#68 — rich planner snapshot (present only when ENABLE_PACKING_PLANNER).

ParsedItemModel.title: ParsedItemModel
ParsedItemModel.description:
Frozen minimal shape (contract §5.2) — every field nullable.

`null` means "not determined", which is distinct from an empty list. Values
come from our own bounded vocabulary (see
`app/application/purchase/candidate_normalizer.py`), never verbatim from the
product page, so this object is safe to put in an LLM prompt.

PreviewFeedbackRequest.title: PreviewFeedbackRequest
PreviewFeedbackRequest.description:
Contract §6.1's frozen feedback body, verbatim.

``{"verdict": "looks_like_me|not_like_me|garment_wrong", "aspects": [...]}``
with ``aspects`` optional. V3-020 sends `{"verdict": "…"}` with the key
**absent**, and that is the shape this must keep accepting.

``extra="forbid"`` is the V3-019 precedent applied to the same threat: the
contract froze two fields, so a client attaching a comment, a score or a
provider hint is rejected with 422 rather than having it silently dropped.
It matters more here than on the create surface, because this endpoint is
the one place a free-text field would be tempting — and
docs/v3-analytics-events.md §5 rules free text out of this signal entirely.

``aspects`` is capped at the size of its own vocabulary: five distinct
values exist, so a longer list is either duplicates (normalized away
server-side) or an attempt to make the field carry volume. Duplicates are
accepted and deduplicated rather than rejected — the client is describing
one render, not submitting a set.

PreviewFeedbackResponse.title: PreviewFeedbackResponse
PreviewFeedbackResponse.description:
What was recorded, echoed back — and nothing else.

Contract §6.1 froze the request body but no response shape, so this is the
minimum that lets a client confirm the stored state after a conflicting
resubmission (`verdict` is the *stored* one, which is the submitted one
under last-write-wins). It carries no `provider`, `model_version` or
`prompt_version`: §6.4 keeps that provenance internal, and this endpoint's
whole purpose is feeding an evaluation the user must not be able to read
the pipeline identity out of.

`recorded_at` is the row's `updated_at`, so an identical resubmission
returns the *original* timestamp — the observable difference between a
no-op and a change of mind.

PurchaseCandidateResponse.title: PurchaseCandidateResponse
PurchaseCandidateResponse.description:
`{id, status, parsed_item}` — contract §5.2.

`parse_failed` is terminal but still decidable: the decision endpoint
(V3-007) then answers `insufficient_information` rather than erroring, and
`parsed_item` still carries whatever partial attributes were recovered so
the client can display and edit them.

PurchaseEvaluation.title: PurchaseEvaluation
PurchaseEvaluation.description: BE#69 — present only when ENABLE_PURCHASE_EVALUATOR; null/empty otherwise.

ReasoningItem.title: ReasoningItem
ReasoningItem.description:
BE#38/#85 — one grounded reason with source provenance.

`type` keys FE rendering (weather / wear_history / style_match / category / fit).
`source` maps to the FE source enum:
  weather_rule / wardrobe_history / preference_memory / style_memory /
  indoor_climate_inference / llm.
`referenced_item_ids` — item UUIDs that directly drove this entry (may be
  empty for whole-look reasons).
`confidence` — high (rule-derived) | medium (heuristic/statistical) |
  low (llm-authored).

Old persisted rows (pre-BE#85) lack source/referenced_item_ids/confidence;
missing keys default to None / [] so legacy dailies never 500.

RecommendationEventRequest.title: RecommendationEventRequest
RecommendationEventRequest.description:
BE#81 — general passive-learning event ingestion. Append-only capture;
it never mutates explicit preferences (OutfitFeedback / FitFeedback).

ResurfaceInsightResponse.title: ResurfaceInsightResponse
ResurfaceInsightResponse.description:
BE#80 — one lightweight "you haven't worn this in a while, and it fits
today" nudge. Absent when there's no genuine candidate (never fabricated).

TodayContextResponse.title: TodayContextResponse
TodayContextResponse.description:
Phase D — context snapshot the engine saw at generation time. Surfaced
only when ENABLE_TODAY_CONTEXT=true; absent on rows generated before
Phase D landed.

boundary_note.title: Boundary Note
boundary_note.description: Fixed copy: this is about the overall look, not a size or fit guarantee.

WardrobeDecisionResponse.title: WardrobeDecisionResponse
WardrobeDecisionResponse.description:
The frozen §5.3 `wardrobe_decision` shape.

Nothing here depends on an avatar or a visual preview: `visual_need` only
suggests whether a preview entry is worth showing, so the no-avatar
experience is complete (V3_SPEC §5.5).

WardrobeHealthInsightItem.title: WardrobeHealthInsightItem
WardrobeHealthInsightItem.description:
A single wardrobe-health insight as i18n-safe codes + numbers.

The backend never returns user-facing copy; the frontend localizes from the
stable ``type`` code and the numeric ``metrics``.

``type`` (stable machine codes):
- ``wear_coverage`` — share of items worn recently.
  ``metrics``: ``{"coverage_ratio": float (0-1), "window_days": int (90)}``
- ``unused_items`` — items not worn within rolling windows.
  ``metrics``: ``{"unused_60": int, "unused_90": int, "unused_180": int}``
- ``category_balance`` — concentration across categories.
  ``metrics``: ``{"dominant_ratio": float (0-1), "counts": {<category>: int}}``;
  empty ``metrics`` ``{}`` when balance can't be computed yet.
- ``data_sparsity`` — emitted only for an empty wardrobe.
  ``metrics``: ``{"item_count": 0}``.

``severity``: stable code ``low`` / ``medium`` / ``high``.

WardrobeHealthResponse.title: WardrobeHealthResponse
WardrobeHealthResponse.description:
Wardrobe health score + insights, fully i18n-safe.

``score``: int 0-100. ``level``: stable code ``great`` / ``good`` /
``fair`` / ``low`` (FE localizes the headline). No baked English summary —
FE renders copy from ``score``, ``level`` and each insight's ``metrics``.
